informed_source_corrections_from_photo: The completion form after እስከ is ተፍጻሜቱ in the selected image: compare the ሚ in እምቀዳሚ on the same physical line (long rightward terminal foot), while completion ሜ has curled return foot; and terminal ቱ has the second rightward spur, unlike sixth-order ት. The photographed lexical lemma is ተፍጻሜት, not identical to the whole body form. Underlying noun means end/completion, and col1389 explicitly cites Hen2:2 under that range. The selected -tu ending may support English “its completion”; firm antecedent for possessive not fixed by the lexical entry. Preserve prior visual freeze as provisional history.
findings: Photographed cols297–299 show the IV,1 appearance verb with the precise imperfect head ይስተርኢ in col298; section1a has making oneself visible, coming into view, appearing of things or persons, not merely active looking or doing. Adjacent derived transitive showing/revealing branch is separate. This does not certify the subject of the clause.

Photographed col778 እንዘ permits circumstantial cum/dum and related senses. Selected line ends እንዘ ይስተርኢ. A guarded “as/while [it/he] appears” or cautious visible/appearance phrase can preserve the selected construction if unresolved subject/attachment are disclosed. Do not assign God or the works as certain or replace with editorial ለከመ on the conjectured omission in notes13–15.

Photographed grammar p512 §197(d) and Dillmann col815 support universal-plus-negative expressing nothing/no one/none, not mechanically “not all”. The exact clause still requires coherent scope explanation and no Greek restoration. Col215 reflexive stem turn/transform supports change.

Dillmann col43 ለበወ understanding/perceiving with actual Hen2:2 citation; col217 earth; cols463–464 prior/beginning; col750 endpoint until; col775 regarding/concerning; cols1165–1166 work/deed including divine works; cols151–152 God. These support the non-crux line structure and both work forms rather than importing a second Greek works clause.
